metaDescription: Six inverter generators from 3,600 to 12,000 watts, ranked as a size ladder so you can match running watts, fuel type and weight to your real loads.
expertTake: The WEN 4800-watt dual fuel is the best all-round rung of this ladder, because it covers a camper, a fridge and a few tools without being a two-person lift. The Oxseryn 4400 is the value pick if you accept an open frame and a louder note. Skip the 12,000-watt tier unless you genuinely plan to feed a transfer switch, because most households never use that much power.
introParagraphs: Inverter generators now span a huge range, from lunchbox units to machines that can feed a sub-panel. The word covers very different tools, so the useful question is which rung of the size ladder matches the loads you actually own.

This guide climbs that ladder one step at a time. At each step you gain running watts, a second fuel and a 240 volt outlet, and you lose portability, quiet and simplicity, so the goal is to stop at the lowest rung that covers your worst-case load.

products.name: WEN 56360i 3600W RV-Ready Inverter Generator
products.description:
Forty-six pounds for 2,900 rated watts is the headline here, and it is an unusually good ratio for a gasoline inverter. The 149cc engine is the same displacement class that runs well-known mid-size units, and the RV-ready label means a 30 amp outlet is on the panel. A fuel shut-off valve is included, which is the single most useful storage feature on any small engine.

This is the rung to choose when the answer to what do I need is a refrigerator, a few lights and a camper. It lacks electric start, a CO sensor and propane, so it stays simple and light. Against the 4,000 rated watts of the WEN 4800 dual fuel, it gives up capacity and a second fuel but saves a noticeable amount of mass and cost.

With a recoil start only, a cold morning means a few honest pulls. Learn the choke and prime sequence at the first oil change rather than during an outage, and keep a fresh can of ethanol-free gas for the first fill of the season.
products.bestFor: A first inverter purchase that needs a camper plug and one-person handling.
pros: Simple recoil-start design with few parts
cons: No CO sensor or electric start

products.name: Oxseryn 4400W Open Frame Inverter Generator

specList.label: Outlets
specList.value: Two 120V, one 12V DC, one RV port

products.description:
Oxseryn takes a different route from the enclosed machines on this list. Its open frame leaves the engine and alternator in view, which keeps the weight and cost down and lets heat escape easily. The price of that design is a louder exhaust note and more exposure to rain and dust.

Output is 3,400 running watts against the 3,600 surge of the entry-level WEN, so it gives meaningfully more usable power than the WEN 56360i while staying in gas-only territory. The 2-gallon tank with a gauge and the listed 14 hours at a quarter load in ECO mode are its strongest points for a long outage.

Owning one means checking the oil often and keeping it under a cover, because open frames pick up debris. Think of it as a workshop or backup-power machine, not a quiet campground companion, and stack it next to the enclosed Westinghouse units if neighbors matter.
products.bestFor: Backup and job-site users who want the most running watts per cost and can live with noise.
pros: 3,400 running watts at a low cost
Two-gallon tank with a fuel gauge
Listed 14 hours at 25% load in ECO
cons: Exposed engine needs a cover outdoors

products.name: WEN 4800W Dual Fuel Electric Start Inverter Generator
products.description:
Four thousand rated watts on both fuels is a rarity, since many dual fuel machines lose a few hundred watts on propane. This WEN lists 4,000 on gasoline and 4,000 on propane, with only the surge dropping from 4,800 to 4,320, so the propane option costs you almost nothing in sustained power. Electric start and an RV-ready panel round out the package.

Weight and money are what the cheaper Oxseryn saves you, but you gain an enclosed case, propane storage that never goes stale and push-button starting. Against the WEN 6800 above it, you lose the 240 volt option and about 1,100 rated watts, while the unit stays much easier to carry.

For ownership, the propane path is the quiet advantage: a propane cylinder can sit for years without the carburetor gumming, so use gas for runs and propane as the long-term stored fuel. Check the propane hose and regulator for cracks each spring.
products.bestFor: Most households that want a camper, fridge and tools covered by one machine with two fuel options.
pros: 4,000 rated watts on both gas and propane
cons: Heavier than the single-fuel entry model

products.name: WEN 6800W Dual Fuel Inverter with CO Watchdog
products.description:
A bonded-neutral 240 volt configuration is the main reason to step up to this machine. It means one outlet can feed 240 volt loads and the listing even mentions low-power Level 2 charging for battery and hybrid electric vehicles. The 224cc engine delivers 5,100 rated watts on gasoline and 4,500 on propane, a drop of about 600 watts that you should plan for.

The WEN Watchdog CO sensor automatically turns the unit off if carbon monoxide builds up, which is a practical safety layer for a machine that people tend to park near a house. Against the Westinghouse 8200 tri-fuel above, it lacks natural gas and a remote key fob but also costs less.

Because 5,100 watts is a lot of engine work, use a dedicated set of heavy extension cords rated for the load and check them for heat after the first hour. Store the unit with the fuel valve closed and give the sensor a test every season by following the manual.
products.bestFor: Homeowners who need 240 volts for a well pump, a small compressor or electric vehicle charging.
cons: Propane output drops by about 600 watts

products.name: Westinghouse iGen8200TFc 8,200W Tri-Fuel Inverter
products.description:
Natural gas is the third fuel that sets this machine apart. If your house has a gas line, a hookup lets the unit run for as long as the utility keeps supplying gas, with no refueling and no stale tanks. The panel also carries a 120/240 volt 50 amp outlet meant for a transfer switch or interlock kit.

Inverter technology changes engine speed with demand, which keeps the engine out of full throttle most of the time and quiets a unit of this size. Compared with the 6,800-watt WEN, it adds natural gas and a remote key fob, and it moves into the range where a central air conditioner is a realistic load.

This is a machine you install and plan around, rather than carry to a campsite. Have a licensed electrician fit the interlock or transfer switch, run it under load twice a year, and keep a short list of which circuits you will feed in an outage.
products.bestFor: Households with a gas line that want fuel-free backup for a few large circuits.
pros: Third fuel option with natural gas
Remote electric start from a key fob
Inverter speed control for quieter running
cons: Too heavy and costly for camping
Needs an electrician for a safe hookup

products.name: Westinghouse iGen12000TFc 12,000W Tri-Fuel Inverter
products.description:
Whole-home backup power is the explicit job of this machine, and the spec sheet reflects it with a 12,000-watt peak and a THD of three percent or less. That clean output matters because modern furnaces, inverter air conditioners and appliance boards care about wave quality more than the older induction motors did.

Insulation and mufflers are the noise strategy, and the listing claims up to fifty percent fuel savings through inverter speed control. That figure compares against a fixed-speed machine, so treat it as a best case rather than a promise. In practice the biggest gain is that the engine throttles down overnight when only a refrigerator and a furnace blower are running.

A unit this size needs a permanent spot, a level pad and a plan for fuel. Natural gas is the easiest sustained path; if you rely on gasoline, plan on several cans and a rotation schedule so none is older than a few months.
products.bestFor: Large homes that want to run central comfort loads through a transfer switch.
pros: Largest running capacity in this ladder
Inverter speed control saves fuel at part load
cons: Very heavy and not a travel machine
Real-world noise is far above small units

buyingCriteria.criterion: Where on the ladder you belong
buyingCriteria.explanation: Add up the running watts of everything you want on at once, then add the biggest single motor start. A fridge, lights and a camper fit under the WEN 56360i at 2,900 rated watts, while a well pump and a furnace need the 5,100 of the WEN 6800 or more. Buying a rung higher than needed costs weight, fuel and noise every single time you use it.

Propane stores indefinitely and burns cleaner, gasoline gives the most power, and natural gas removes refueling. The WEN 4800 gives 4,000 watts on both gas and propane, while the WEN 6800 drops from 5,100 to 4,500 on propane. Match the fuel to how long an outage is likely to last in your area.

A 240 volt outlet is required for well pumps, large compressors and many home-backup transfer switches. The WEN 6800 offers a bonded-neutral 240 volt configuration, and the Westinghouse 8200 and 12000 add a 50 amp outlet. Smaller units like the Oxseryn only supply 120 volts, which is fine for camping but limiting for a house.

An enclosed case directs sound through baffles and keeps rain and dust off the engine, while an open frame is cheaper and cools easily but is louder. The Oxseryn 4400 is open frame, and the WEN and Westinghouse units are enclosed. Match the style to where the machine will sit and who lives next door.

Recoil start is simple but unwelcome in a storm, while electric and remote start turn a stressful outage into a button press. The WEN 56360i is recoil only, the WEN 4800 and 6800 add electric start, and the Westinghouse units add a key fob. Battery-backed start systems need a maintained battery, so factor in a trickle charger.

A CO shutdown sensor, low-oil shutdown and overload protection protect people and engines. The WEN 6800 includes its Watchdog sensor, while the Oxseryn lists low oil and overload protection only. A sensor is a last line of defense and never a reason to run a generator near a window.

specDecoder.meaning: Surge is a few seconds of overshoot and rated is what the machine holds for hours. The gap grows on larger models.
specDecoder.watchFor: The WEN 6800 lists 6,800 surge but only 5,100 rated on gasoline.

specDecoder.meaning: Cubic centimeters describe engine size, and larger engines usually make more power at lower revs. Displacement alone does not say how well a machine is built.
specDecoder.watchFor: The 224cc engine in the WEN 4800 and 6800 is shared across two rated outputs, so check the rating, not the cc.

specDecoder.meaning: A bonded neutral ties the neutral conductor to the frame and is what lets a generator feed 240 volt equipment directly. It must be set correctly when connecting to a house.
specDecoder.watchFor: The WEN 6800 is bonded neutral, so do not plug it into a house panel without an interlock or transfer switch.

specDecoder.meaning: A listing that claims a long run time usually measures it at a quarter load with eco mode on. Heavier loads shorten the number sharply.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Oxseryn lists 14 hours at 25% load, and a half-load figure would be much shorter.

specDecoder.meaning: Total harmonic distortion measures how clean the sine wave is, with lower being better for electronics. Under three percent is the usual inverter benchmark.
specDecoder.watchFor: The iGen12000TFc lists three percent or less, a clear sign that it targets modern appliances.

howWeEvaluated.title: Rated watts on each fuel
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared running watts for every fuel the machine accepts, not just the headline number. The WEN 4800 holds 4,000 on both gas and propane, while the WEN 6800 drops from 5,100 to 4,500. Machines that hide the propane figure were marked down.

howWeEvaluated.title: Weight per rated watt
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at how much machine you carry for each rated watt, because that ratio predicts whether you will actually use it. The WEN 56360i at 46 pounds and 2,900 rated watts is the efficiency benchmark. The 12,000-watt tri-fuel naturally sits at the other end.

howWeEvaluated.title: Output connections
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked whether the panel offers a 30A RV outlet, a 240 volt outlet or a 50 amp outlet, because the plug decides what you can actually connect. The Westinghouse 8200 and 12000 lead with a 50A outlet. The Oxseryn only offers 120 volt plugs and an RV port.

howWeEvaluated.title: Start system and fuel flexibility
howWeEvaluated.description: We counted start methods and fuels, since a stressful outage punishes a hard-to-start machine. Remote start and electric start rank above recoil only. Natural gas adds a fuel that does not need refilling.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ownership burden
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at storage features such as a fuel shut-off, propane for long storage and parts availability. Brands with dealer service or clear parts diagrams scored higher, while open-frame machines needed a covered storage spot.

cards.label: Enclosed inverter
cards.text: The WEN and Westinghouse machines keep the engine inside a baffled case, which lowers the exhaust note and shields the engine from rain. They cost more per running watt and weigh more for the output.

cards.label: Open frame
cards.text: The Oxseryn 4400 exposes its engine, which saves weight and cost and cools easily. It suits a workshop or garage patio but not a campground with quiet hours.

howToChoose.note: Choose enclosed if neighbors or campsite rules matter, and open frame if cost per watt is the priority.

rows: Fewer parts and a lower weight
Same rated watts on both fuels
Gas, propane and a bigger load
No refueling during a long outage

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A 50 amp outlet or transfer-switch readiness, low THD and a fuel you can sustain. Plan the circuits you will feed before choosing the size.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Westinghouse iGen8200TFc covers a furnace and several circuits with a natural gas option, and the iGen12000TFc adds capacity for a central air conditioner.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You need 240 volts, a natural gas hookup or remote start. The WEN 6800 and the Westinghouse tri-fuel units provide those features, and each rung adds real utility.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Your loads are a fridge, lights and a camper. The WEN 56360i or the Oxseryn 4400 covers that at far lower cost and weight.

maintenance.interval: After the first 20 hours, then yearly or per the manual
maintenance.why: Larger crankcases still run hot under load. Fresh oil protects the bearings and keeps the low-oil sensor from tripping.
A monthly run exercises the starter, battery and carburetor. It also reveals a weak extension cord before an outage.
Ethanol absorbs water and gums jets. On a dual fuel machine, run the carburetor dry on gas and store propane separately.
Electric and remote start rely on a small battery. A trickle charger keeps it ready for the day you need it.
Propane hoses and natural gas fittings crack with age. Replace any hose with surface cracks.

faq.q: How many watts do I need for a typical home outage?
faq.a: A refrigerator, lights, a furnace blower and chargers usually fit inside 3,000 to 4,000 running watts. Adding a well pump or an air conditioner pushes you into the 5,000 watt range or higher.

Yes if you want to store fuel for years, since propane does not go stale. Check the propane rating first, because the WEN 6800 loses about 600 watts on propane while the WEN 4800 loses none in sustained output.

faq.q: Can I connect a large inverter generator directly to my house?
faq.a: Only through a properly installed transfer switch or interlock kit. Backfeeding through a dryer outlet can injure utility workers and is illegal in most areas.
They deliver clean power at a low cost, but they run louder and are more exposed to weather. The Oxseryn 4400 fits a workshop or backup role better than a campground.

faq.q: Do bigger inverters use more fuel at idle?
faq.a: They burn less at light load than a conventional machine, since the engine throttles down. Fuel use still rises quickly with load, so size close to your real needs.

faq.q: Should I worry about carbon monoxide?
faq.a: Yes. Always run any generator outdoors and well away from the house, and treat a built-in sensor such as the WEN Watchdog as a backup, not a guarantee.
